I am 69 years old now, and this small plot of 0.06 hectare is where I plant my cassava with some yam and maize in between. I went to school some, so I can read the writing on a fertilizer bag, but I also know that one full bag of NPK is too much money for this tiny piece of land, and it is meant for bigger plots. I will spread goat and chicken manure from behind my house instead, because I own this land and I want to keep it fertile. I am using my own cassava cuttings that I kept from last harvest — I will not buy those improved ones until I see my neighbor's plot do well with them. We have plenty of rain here in the South South, so I do not need to water it, and I will pull weeds with my hands rather than buy spray. My family will work about 14 days on this plot from clearing to harvest, and I will hire two young men for two days to help me cut the bush because my back is not strong like before.
